description: Sequential local components. covers records partial contribution, never proof of full SEC closure. Candidate package kernels are supplementary; fixed control integration oracles decide boundaries.
prerequisites: Node 22 executable launches this test and all children; VEXA_CANDIDATE points to a disjoint immutable candidate.
Docker and local images/dependency artifacts required by the existing harnesses must already be available. Components reuse those harnesses without weakening their prerequisites.
Candidate package kernels resolve dependencies from the candidate snapshot; prepare dependencies outside canonical before execution.
The reviewed HTTP component must be integrated into this control snapshot before the runner starts. Its absence fails preflight.
Coverage gaps below are blocking requirements, not optional exclusions; full PASS is impossible until reviewed controls close them.
Python 3 is needed by the unchanged email/push pre-send SQL controllers; history/imports additionally require the existing local browser image.

components.note: Existing full ENTRYDIRECT exam includes F02-05 and F02-06 inventory plus three mutation controls and cleanup; do not duplicate F02-06 execution. Historical intermittent postcommit barrier remains an execution risk.

Control copy of existing author runtime retains all seven steps and adds SQL publication hashes/provider-call counts around owner revocation. Wrapper validates publication receipt and cleanup, with owned-journal recovery after failed termination. Candidate harness/config dependencies remain recorded; no independent acceptance inferred. Six in-memory fixture calibrations precede the seven-step runtime wrapper; exact EU synthetic transport does not contact external providers.

exclusions: No reuse of an earlier capacity result, production deployment or security acceptance.
Historical UI suites explorer/outbox/email/push are not rerun with known stale labels; omitted boundaries remain coverageGaps.
SQL and Storage are local real services; gateway kernels use synthetic provider transports, not live model execution.
Existing signed download URLs require a separately authorized transition; new emission denial does not invalidate them.

coverageNotes.scope: Real consumeNotification plus real SQL outbox and local HTTP sink, in-app publication, and provider-specific SQL pre-send controls. No claim of SMTP/push delivery or external account validation. Execution and independent acceptance remain required.

coverageDesign.design: Actual context assembly and validation reject a real foreign redacted revision despite identical hostile text; roles separated, fetch destinations and logs observed. Synthetic model output, no live-model semantics claimed.
Same URL owner/viewer/B, revoked membership and browser logout with old cookie/tab/back. BFCache only when observed; no instantaneous idle DOM erase claimed.
Build canaries before compilation, published artifacts/responses/logs plus authenticated JSON/HTML brief bytes and headers. Other export families and log destinations not universally claimed.
Signed raw HTTP reaches real tenant-bound SQL receipt and wakeup; replay, forged binding and revoked authority have no unauthorized receipt.
Contract requires local real jobs/notification authorization, covered by SQL plus actual consumer and SYN loopback; external provider delivery is outside local scope.

staticReviews.conclusion: Connector payload attachment URLs are not fetched. CRM destinations/paths are constructed and validated; Storage uses configured server and tenant-scoped object paths. Gateway treats URLs as data.
limits: Static data-flow review; no dynamic DNS or external infrastructure proof
Recovery SDK wrapper has no explicit redirect prohibition; no payload-controlled attachment destination found
